[*] Meddigagoe digital flipbook animation dots now have a collision detector that displays an off white background between the frames to reduce flicker. Before the color matched the dark grey background  of the overall composition.

[*] Preloading artwork added. This is seen before the main title screen. The idea is that we are seeing the formation of the microscope interface that will be ready to use at the end of the loading sequence. This is  generative artwork in that it changes and is totally different every time Integument is launched.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/e02379bffbb198387cc7d202362f5c5359c21160.png[/img]
[*] New Spot Illustration added. This replaces a previous one. Spot illustrations had their vibrance boosted to reflect and balance the overall color changes across Integument and its DLC.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/a761300586efae0d6d0fbd6d8c07f331a244d04c.png[/img]
[*] The new spot illustration comes with new blortus anatomical diagrams that include labeled features and an audio lab note.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/d4bbb4f559d1717da22f1fe8e1d95a84558e3569.png[/img]
[*] There is also more real-time animation of information being transferred between the blortus and the DNA base pair molecules.  I tend to save this kind of thing for the DLC since I want this to still be considered an illustration, though obviously it's something else. However, this particular piece really needed to have the special treatment primarily because of the human reference :)
[*] Main window will now revert normal status after syncing. Before it was still displaying "SYNC 100%" after completion.
[*] Real-time animated progress strip added beneath the "mematron" signature.  This replaces the base pair generator. I found this to be more interesting.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/e189dfa79f0ffd72f2c5f70e2b15301393c614d5.png[/img]
[*] Added more detail to across several traces. Some of them connect to the progress strip.
[/olist]
[h1]FIXES[/h1]
Window icon flashing fixed. It was flickering in the taskbar and window border. The reference to it in the code was in the wrong place.

[h1]Artist's Notes[/h1]
The year was 1982 and I was 12 years old. Even then my attraction to computer graphics was strong. I would draw all of my work on grid paper and label the grid lines with horizontal and vertical number coordinates. Once these numbers were entered into my computer and run, an exact copy of what was on paper would appear on screen.

That experience is what prepared me for making the preload (generative) art. The process is the same except that I go straight to the computer without the need to first graph it out.

The preloading artwork also reminds me of the type of art I made in foundation color theory and 2D design courses with colored pencils.

In making it I had to write the X and Y position and shape of everything to be shown. In our case it's a basic line drawing of the Integument interface. For example, one of those positions looks like, "rect(1060.0, 44.0, 228.0, 606.0)" meaning draw something here and make it this size.  The first 2 parts are x/y and the last 2 are the width/height. Put enough of these together and a image is made.

But the reason why this is kind of a big deal is because at this point you should not be able to see anything but a blank screen.  That's where a combination of formal training and self-teaching come into play. 

The ability to learn how to learn.

notes.title: Hada Microbiome Area Scan 04: ACTIVATED!, New loading screen art and more.
notes.notes:
[h1]Hada Microbiome Area Scan 04: ACTIVATED![/h1]
[olist]
[*] [b]New detailed illustrations[/b] of hada predator called a, Meddigagoe. These are the same creatures in hot pursuit of the blortuses/blorta on the main screen (hood).  This new screen has some slick interactivity coming from technology used for the DLC.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/a8f9bcf115a778f813bb97508fec3768e91de631.png[/img]
[*] [b]Spot illustration buttons[/b] have enhanced looks.  Design cues from their contents has been carried around them.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/08ef6570cad028e7791d198bb741e9385d4b0466.png[/img]
[*] [b]More details[/b] near and the 4 Spot illustrations to balance out the additional color shapes near the spot illustrations.
[*] [b]Spot illustration buttons[/b] will now activate after a mouse click instead of a mouse press. This prevents accidental launching of multiple windows with a long mouse press.
[/olist]

[h1]Features[/h1]
[olist]
[*] [b]Integument preload screen[/b] changed from black to a soft dark blue.
[*] [b]Loading percentage animation[/b] in outer window frames.
[*] Integument [b]new splash screen[/b].  This was done to reflect and connect the current design language.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/c33795b81efc2c696f98dbffe06c1c10051f25da.png[/img]
[*] [b]Meddigagoe run cycle[/b] in the lower level interface (engine) was changed from a movie of an animation loop to a real-time animation loop.  Calculating  frames can sometimes be less resource intensive than playing a movie file.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/442fbb8af347aafc58704da9cd3db7838e7bbe4c.png[/img]
[*] [b]The Data Stack Screen[/b] (DSS), Animation color grid no longer is always on but will only turn on when you mouse over it.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/cb335a41bec6cc4a6b8f166408af15cf6b00342a.png[/img]
[*] [b]Mematron signature[/b] When clicked the music playing will have a visual indicator that will stop its animation once the music has stopped.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/97f6e1950e09ccce3bc4e9144a901a64bce89251.png[/img]
[*] [b]Meddigagoe and blortus technical readouts[/b] are all now tidied up. These are the small colorful blinking texts on the sides of some of the windows. They where not lined up perfectly.  This all hand coded so yes, it was a pain to do but it was really getting on my nerves!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/72695f11a974a1f5c2431a4f28c05708cd0b6071.png[/img]
[*] [b]Personal Log 01[/b]: interface now displays a very cool / atypical waveform when the log entry is being played.  Once the personal log has stopped playing the play indicator and waveform will automatically turn off. The lights used to stay on even after the recording had ended.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/97d6684a50e3d65963eea934cc10781e6f1c9bc8.png[/img]
[*] [b]TBN (Translation Buffer Node)[/b] The rotating thingamabob located in the middle of the "engine" (Lower level screen interface).  One of the orbital nodes was brought back into orbit. It had been rotating around the center of the Data sphere off screen. In cleaning up my code this was revealed.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/672f76fae58b92b80349ac2297b030eae44b20fd.png[/img]
[*] Traces added along the bottom and left side of the engine (Lower level screen interface). Yes, these pixel size dotted lines work just like the traces on circuit boards. Traces carry signals to where they are needed. So feel free to follow them to discover patterns.
[/olist]
[h2]Slightly technical[/h2]
I refactored all 5961 lines of code that make up, "Integument." This is the programmer equivalent of Spring Cleaning.  It's a lot of work but it makes it easier to introduce new content.  This isn't a new thing as I rewrite portions of it  between updates.  It allows me to solve problems, answer questions and discover new things that in turn cause problems, present new questions and challenges.

In the end I hope that this update will have made for a smoother running, more interesting composition.  Remember, this is art for art's sake.

[h1]Did you know?[/h1]
Excluding the obvious, all the the interfaces are hand pixelled with some of it even being created on the fly via code?

notes.title: "Integument - Gates: Database" DLC Field Notes
notes.notes:
[h1]FIELD NOTES[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/a4f08a3933d1cd0363347f0bb9978916acccdbeb.png[/img]
Field notes are a way to experience first thoughts and impressions as an experiment happens.  In these first 9 entries, interactions between Gates and several other hada were observed. In particular, is the largest seen to date called an, Igler. 

This was an unexpected observation as the primary subject is Gates.  However, her relation to Iglers is tied to the Thyim and even the Meddigagoes seen during the experiment.  They are all connected in ways that are not fully understood, but that knowledge base begins with Field Notes.

In addition to the images, you'll be able to view a brief report that includes the name of the researcher, what was seen and the tools used in the experiment.

[h1]FEATURES[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Voiceovers - Accompanying every illustration is a unique voiceover of a scientist that gives context to what's being presented.
[*] 10 Highly detailed, interactive, illustrations. They occupy most of the window.
[*] New rendering techniques used to emphasize color and detail. A strong effort was made to push the design language forward while maintaining color harmony. 
[*] User activated generative animations. A long press on one of the illustrations makes cool things happen.
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/73694d15b967209133da6ef2b1761a66a6cb10d4.png[/img]
The Field Notes button is located 3rd from the top on the left of the "Integument - Gates: Database" interface.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/668987203542aa21e478d7343d6b026bef9257a1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/03a80716953e1fd259d2d1b6d9461f546596343d.png[/img]
The button will change to a "3" when clicked on.  You may also interact with the "Field Notes" button by pressing the "3" key on your keyboard.  (HINT: This like many other things in the DLC and the base application, "Integument" can be activated with a simple key press. Indeed, it's time for you to become a keyboard warrior.) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/2918dda0d40c7687ba8194e467c9863886e65206.png[/img]
Although we are on the surface of the skin, the magnification is so high that we're starting to see the building blocks of life; DNA nucleotides.  What do you think about that nerds?!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/8c482c6827acf594ebce9d5090f1a2a045be6f8a.png[/img]
This size chart does matter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/5682d5d22274bbaaf5aff2aecacd4d5f820c8572.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/8fd0b67688456d82a9ca7ef2e526771855b96d3e.png[/img]
"M, M, M, M.A.S.K."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/5adf9ac124d79e4c6f83798a08806c223af3775d.png[/img]
Shaken, not stirred.

[h1]OTHER CHANGES[/h1]
[FIXED] There were 4 pixels missing from the upper left corner of the main window.
[CODE] Custom code written to allow a ton of nested windows.  
[CODE] Buttons that activate and deactivate after they are done doing what they need to do.
[CODE] Graphical elements can be persistent or turned off without affecting the entire application.

[h1]FUN FACTS[/h1]
[list]
[*] At 15 nm (nano meters/metres) Gates is considered very tall for a hada.  An Igler is 150 nm. By comparison, a single human blood cell is 10,000 nm.  Now that's big on a small scale!
[*] If Gates can be considered the cleaner fish of the Hada Kingdom, then an Igler is like a Blue Whale.  The largest of it's kind.
[/list]

[h1]ABOUT THIS DLC[/h1]
Database: Gates represents more focused analyses.  This is the foundation for more detailed content, some of which is hinted in the base application, "Integument."

notes.title: DLC DATABASE EXPANSION
notes.notes:
[h1]Integument - Database: Gates DLC, Database Expansion[/h1]

The Database: Gates DLC, represents a more focused analysis of an interesting hada called, Gates.

This lays the groundwork for more unique content within the Integument - Database: Gates DLC.  It started off as being visually compact in comparison to the base "Integument" application.  I decided to make it bigger because it allows me to show off more experimental techniques.

Changes include:
[olist]
[*] Integument - Database: Gates DLC was made 50% bigger (from 672x704 to 1343x704) to introduce and inspire more content.
[*] New Title Screen. This is to reflect the new size of the DLC.
[*] Cursor is now a crosshair.
[*] Several new highly detailed illustrations have been created. Some of the new design language from the base Integument application was integrated and used as inspiration.
[*] The small skin cutaway view was replaced with a higher quality version. Thanks to recent artwork that was made for, "Integument." 
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/e75767532fa70e2e7c73110d1f929b3114751b40.png[/img]

notes.title: Visual and not so visual update
notes.notes:
Lots of minor changes across the board.  These affect the GUI and the underlying code for "Integument" and "Integument - Database: Gates DLC." 

Changes made to, Integument:
[olist]
[*]Many small texts made a bit more readable.
[*]Rotating data wheel in the middle of the "Engine" is now interactive with new art.  New animations and design inspired by a time piece.  It represents the intersection between the pure data and the start of the sorting process.  This was fun to make, so pretty in an industrial designer type way.
[*]B/W Meddigagoe keyframe run animation is consistent. This is the only animation that's not being made in real-time. It's somewhat interactive too.
[*]Text display of DNA base pairs (Base pair generator).
[*]User login name "mematron" moved to the top of the screen.
[*]New music added.  You'll have to search for it.
[*]Added code to cleanly shutdown Java processes specifically used for when Integument is run. Not quite a memory leak but it had the same effect. As Han Solo says, "It's not my fault!"
[*]Minor animation added to Spot Illustration 01.
[*]Most of the green and blue memory cells are now active. What's a "memory cell?!"  You'll figure it out. I trust you ːsteamthumbsupː

[*]Added several small illustrations to introduce more color variations. This also represents the idea that the computer system is processing new types information and changing it's appearance to reflect that.
[/olist]

notes.title: Hada Microbiome Area Scan 01: ACTIVATED!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43321244/cd2a6eee4b6c965019f32bbf37a68e0800575766.png[/img]
The addition of a button to access, Hada Microbiome Area Scan 01. This reveals a snapshot of a preliminary scan of a human face. It's purpose is to locate, identify and catalog unique Hada lifeforms.  You may access this new information by clicking on the colorized spot illustration at the bottom of the interface (Engine) and to the left of the "Personal Log 01" buttons.

Over time this information will unpack to reveal more detail.
